reviewer: Codex root (AI-assisted supplied-English curation for 2 Samuel 8–12)
review_method: Read every complete actual source unit and every retained target and necessary context from the pinned Saints English texts. Independently reread all 114 complete source/target/category/rationale triples in four untruncated slices (1–29,30–58,59–87,88–114); the first slice was explicitly redisplayed after an earlier output was lost to context truncation. Preserved the original draft and fifteen exact explanation/category refinements, and separately reread all fifteen corrected complete triples. Comparisons use concrete shared clauses, stated people/objects/counts, particular commands and responses, narrative contrasts and meaningful labelled local literary relationships. Differing names, parentage, roles, numbers, object labels, agency and speech-versus-event status are preserved. This is an initial curated supplied-English pass, not exhaustive discovery, new Greek/Hebrew/apparatus work, independent human specialist review, medical diagnosis, modern site mapping or solved historical harmonization.
pin_method: Fresh fixed-commit raw fetches of all eight retained source/target books, exact Git blob rehash against the saved fixed-commit registry and complete parsed cache equality. Raw and normalized-cache byte differences recorded separately; technical checks add no review credit.

old_row.relationship: Moab's defeat and gift-bearing service in parallel summaries
old_row.rationale: Both state that David struck Moab and Moab became his servants bringing gifts; Samuel additionally gives two measured lengths killed and two kept alive, which are not replaced with a different ratio.

new_row.relationship: Moab's defeat and gift-bearing service in parallel summaries
new_row.rationale: Both state that David struck Moab and Moab became his servants bringing gifts; Samuel additionally assigns two measured lengths to death and keeps two measured lengths alive, which are not replaced with a different ratio.

unresolved_candidates.reason: The complete actual 8:17 lists Ahimelech son of Abiathar as priest, while 1 Samuel30:7 identifies Abiathar the priest as son of Ahimelech. Both passages and their contexts were read; the parentage is not independently reversed, silently substituted or declared a textual mistake. The retained8:17 link compares only the explicit Zadok-priest role with2 Samuel20:25.

candidate_exclusions.proposed_claim: Independently certify every differing personal/place/object name in parallel accounts, harmonize figures or actors, supply half-beard wording, fourfold restitution, omitted speech, a newly resolved pronoun, or a reconstructed forced-labour/execution method for Samuel12:31.
candidate_exclusions.reason: Only bounded actual shared clauses and explicit contrasts are retained; original wording and the different accounts remain visible. No completion credit is assigned to excluded equivalence or harmonization claims.

editorial_notes.note: Preserve the actual two measured lengths for death and two alive in8:2; armlets, collars and spears/shields as distinct object descriptions; David versus Abessa and Gaimale versus Valley of Salts in8:13; Benaiah counselor and palace officials in8:18; the Jonathan-son Mephibosheth; Chalamak/Ailam and distinct Syrian troop figures; Eliab parentage, full repeated11:22 speech, sevenfold12:6, Idedi and unassigned pronouns, repeated first-capture language and Melchol their king. Partial parallels do not resolve every genealogy, site, chronology or treatment method.
